 Judgment

The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.386/2016 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Kozhikode, is the appellant in MACA No.3952/2018 and the 3rd respondent in the OP is the appellant in MACA No.3475/2018.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 31.10.2015.

According to the petitioner, on 31.10.2015 at about 8 a.m., while he was riding a motorcycle, a tipper lorry bearing reg.no.KL-57-A-6211 driven by the 2 nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner,
Sajith vs Reliance General Insurance Co.Limited on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93503251/
2 hit against the motorcycle and as a result of which, he fell down and sustained serious injuries.

entities.text: Sajith vs Reliance General Insurance Co.Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Because of the injuries sustained in the accident, his right leg below knee was amputated.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the 2025:KER:31456 MACA NO.3952 OF 2018 & MACA NO.3475 OF 2018 offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.50,00,000/-.
4.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimonies of PWs 1 and 2 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A12, X1 and C1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.18,42,700/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner and 3rd respondent preferred these appeals.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri.A.V.M. Salahuddeen, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri. P.Jacob Mathew, the learned Standing 2025:KER:31456 MACA NO.3952 OF 2018 & MACA NO.3475 OF 2018 Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
According to the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the 3rd respondent, the functional disability of the petitioner fixed by the Tribunal at 80% is on the higher side.
She would also argue that, since it was a head on collision between the two vehicles, 50% contribution is to be found against the petitioner.

On the other hand, the learned counsel for the petitioner would argue that the notional income of the petitioner fixed by the Tribunal is on the lower side and according to him, since the petitioner was an industrial worker, his functional disability is to be taken as 100%.
11.
According to the petitioner, he is an industrial worker getting a daily income of Rs.600/- per day.
The Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.10,000/-.
In order to prove the income of the petitioner he had relied upon the evidence of PW2 and Ext.A8 salary certificate.
When PW2 was examined, he deposed that the petitioner used to get Rs.600/- per day.
However, in addition to Ext.A8 salary certificate, no other documents were produced to substantiate the evidence of PW2.

It was in the above context, the 2025:KER:31456 MACA NO.3952 OF 2018 & MACA NO.3475 OF 2018 Sajith vs Reliance General Insurance Co.Limited on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93503251/

entities.text: Sajith vs Reliance General Insurance Co.Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
3 Tribunal fixed his notional income at Rs.10,000/-.
12.

As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2015 will come to Rs.10,000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore considering the fact that the petitioner was an industrial worker, his notional income is fixed at Rs.12,000/-.

13. In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
1. Mangled right foot.
2. Bone loss in the mid foot and heel.
3. Medial malleolus undisplaced fracture (L) and right open knee.
14. As per Exhibit C1 disability certificate the petitioner suffered 60% permanent physical disability.
It was issued by the Medical Board attached to Medical College Hospital, Kozhikode.

However, the Tribunal, has fixed his functional disability at 80%.
15.
In respect of the accident, the police registered Crime No.789/2015.
Ext.A1 is the copy of the FIR and Ext.A3 is the Final Report.
As per Ext.A3, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the 2 nd respondent.
There is absolutely no evidence to prove that there was any contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Therefore, there is no merits in the argument advanced by the learned counsel for the 3 rd respondent that there was contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.

16. The learned counsel for the petitioner relying upon the decision of a Single Bench of this Court in Sreejith vs. Azeez and another in MFA (ECC) No.85/2018, would argue that in the case of a head load worker whose leg below knee was amputated, this Court has taken the functional disability at 100% and as such in this case also functional disability of the petitioner is to be taken as 100%.

entities.text: Sreejith vs. Azeez and another in MFA (ECC) No.85/2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
17. The learned counsel has also relied upon Section 2(1)(l) of the Employees Compensation Act,
which defines the term "Total disablement"
as follows:
(l) "total disablement" means such disablement, whether of a temporary or permanent nature, as incapacitates a *[employee] for all work which he was capable of performing at the time of the accident resulting in such disablement:
Provided that permanent total disablement shall be deemed to result from every injury specified in Part I of 2025:KER:31456 MACA NO.3952 OF 2018 & MACA Sajith vs Reliance General Insurance Co.Limited on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93503251/
4 NO.3475 OF 2018 Schedule I or from any combination of injuries specified in Part II thereof where the aggregate percentage of the loss of earning capacity, as specified in the said Part II against those injuries, amounts to one hundred per cent. or more;
18.

entities.text: MACA Sajith vs Reliance General Insurance Co.Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, the learned counsel for the insurer would argue that as per the 1st schedule to the act, in case of amputation below knee, the loss of earning capacity will be only between 50 and 60 percentage.
It is to be noted that while assessing the compensation for loss of disability, what is to be considered is the functional disability and not the physical disability of the petitioner.

Even in the decision in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar [2011 (1) KLT 620(SC)] the Apex court held that the functional disability of the victim depends upon the nature of the job of the victim and that it need not be equal to the physical disability.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar [2011 (1) KLT 620(SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the petitioner is an industrial worker and since his right leg below knee was amputated, he was practically incapacitated from continuing his job as an industrial worker.
At the same time, he may be able to do some other job, which does not require physical labour.
In the above circumstances, I hold that the functional disability of the petitioner can be fixed at 90%.
19. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 26 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 17, as held in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd v. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.30,84,480/-.
20 . Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded Rs.60000/- being the income for 6 months @Rs.10000/-.

Since the notional income of the petitioner is re-fixed at Rs.12000/-, towards loss of earning he is entitled to get a sum of Rs.72000/-(12000 x 6 months)
21.
Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.50000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.50000/- was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
22. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 25 days.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings' and 'loss of amenities of life' are on the lower side and 2025:KER:31456 MACA NO.3952 OF 2018 & MACA NO.3475 OF 2018 hence they are enhanced to Rs.1,50,000/-,
Rs.3,00,000/-.
23.
The learned counsel for the petitioner would argue that the Tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards the cost of prosthesis.
The petitioner has not produced any documents to prove the expense required for purchase of prosthesis.

In the decision in Vivek G. v. National Insurance Company Ltd. 2023 KHC 2941, in the case of a 12 year old child, whose right leg was amputated in an accident in the year 2011, the Hon'ble Apex Court has awarded a total sum of Sajith vs Reliance General Insurance Co.Limited on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93503251/
5 Rs.26,00,000/- towards the cost of 4 prosthesis and the cost of it's maintenance.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the instant case,
the petitioner has not produced any documents to prove the amount required for the purchase of prosthesis.
Wide range of varieties of prosthesis are available in the market.
Therefore, considering the facts I hold that a consolidated sum of Rs.10 lakhs can be awarded towards the cost of prosthesis and the cost of it's maintenance.
24. The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal at 9% is on the higher side.
Considering the facts, I hold that interest at 8% will be a reasonable rate of interest in this case.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

26. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.46,57,680/-,
